Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MedTech Innovations Inc. First Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Sarah Kline, CEO; David Patel, CFO; and Lisa Chen, Chief Technology Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Kline.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. MedTech Innovations delivered solid results this quarter, driven by strong execution and continued demand for our innovative medical device solutions.

Today, I will cover four key aspects of our performance: strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter; competitive dynamics and market share trends; inventory management and working capital optimization; and FDA approvals and CE marks obtained. David will provide additional color on some of these, and he'll follow up with a detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with our strategic priorities and focus areas for the upcoming quarter. David, would you kick us off?

David Patel:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. As we wrap up a strong Q1 where we delivered 14% year-over-year revenue growth to $1.2 billion—driven by 18% expansion in our structural heart franchise and 22% in neuromodulation—let me outline our strategic priorities and key focus areas for Q2. Our playbook remains centered on three pillars: accelerating innovation in high-growth segments, optimizing our global commercial footprint amid macroeconomic headwinds, and driving sustainable margin expansion through operational discipline. These initiatives are designed to sustain our mid-teens organic growth trajectory while navigating reimbursement dynamics and supply chain normalization following the lingering effects of Red Sea disruptions.

First, we're advancing our innovation pipeline with a sharp focus on robotics and AI-enabled devices. Innovation is the lifeblood of MedTech Innovations, and we're doubling down on next-generation platforms to capture share in the $50 billion-plus robotics and digital surgery market, where penetration remains below 20% in most procedures. In Q2, our top initiative is the limited market release of the PrecisionNav 3.0 robotic-assisted navigation system for spinal procedures—a direct competitor to Medtronic's Mazor X and Zimmer Biomet's ROSA platform. Building on our Q1 FDA 510(k) clearance, we'll target 50 initial installs across top-tier U.S. spine centers, aiming for a 25% attach rate to our existing portfolio. Early modeling suggests this could add $45 million in incremental revenue by year-end, with gross margins north of 75% due to our proprietary AI algorithms for real-time 3D imaging fusion.

Complementing this, we're allocating an additional $120 million—or 12% of Q2 revenues—to R&D, prioritizing AI integration in our cardiovascular portfolio. Specifically, we're advancing our Sentinel FLX Pro LAA occluder with embedded machine learning for procedural optimization, mirroring the successful Watchman ecosystem. We expect this to drive a 15% uplift in U.S. structural heart procedure volumes, capitalizing on the aging Baby Boomer demographic where atrial fibrillation prevalence is climbing 7% annually. In parallel, our neuromodulation team is on track for CE Mark submission under the EU MDR framework for the next-gen ReviX recharge-free SCS system, addressing chronic pain in a market growing at 11% CAGR.

Second, on geographic expansion and commercial execution, we're sharpening our focus to balance mature market penetration with emerging growth. The U.S., which accounted for 62% of Q1 revenues at $745 million, remains our anchor—expecting 16% growth in Q2 fueled by a ramp in elective procedures now that hospital capacity utilization has stabilized at 85%. We'll deploy an additional 150 specialized reps in our Value Analysis Committee acceleration program, targeting 75% win rates on RFPs for our TAVR valves in competition with Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platform.

In EMEA, representing 24% of revenues, we're navigating MDR headwinds head-on with a dedicated 20-person regulatory task force. Q2 priorities include 30% volume growth in Germany and the UK via our partnership with Siemens Healthineers for integrated imaging solutions, offsetting a modest 2% reimbursement haircut from the UK's NICE guidelines. APAC, our fastest-growing region at 28% YoY in Q1, will see aggressive expansion: We're committing $50 million to scale manufacturing in our new Suzhou, China facility, aiming to localize 40% of production for cardiac rhythm management devices. This positions us to capture 12% market share in China's $15 billion device market by 2025, leveraging the National Reimbursement Drug List inclusions for our ICDs and riding the 20% procedural growth tailwind from rising diabetes and hypertension burdens.

Emerging markets like LATAM and India get a dedicated focus too—$25 million in targeted investments for distributor network buildout, projecting 35% growth as we introduce low-cost versions of our AccuFlow drug-eluting stents.

Third, on operational excellence and margin discipline, to support this growth, we're laser-focused on supply chain resilience and cost efficiencies. Q1 adjusted gross margins hit 68.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year, thanks to our multi-sourcing strategy that reduced reliance on single Asian suppliers by 30%. In Q2, we'll execute Phase 2 of our MedTech Lean initiative, targeting another 150 basis points expansion to 69.7% through automation in our Galway, Ireland plant—mirroring Stryker's iSuite model—and hedging 80% of raw material exposure amid tantalum price volatility up 15% year-to-date.

SG&A as a percentage of revenue will compress to 32% via zero-based budgeting and our Salesforce optimization, yielding $60 million in run-rate savings. We're also advancing ESG priorities with a 25% reduction in Scope 1 emissions via our new solar-powered facility in Costa Rica, aligning with investor demands and unlocking EU Green Deal incentives.

Looking ahead, these priorities position us to outperform in a market where consensus expects flat-to-2% medtech growth amid inflation and staffing shortages. We're guiding Q2 revenues to $1.28-$1.32 billion, implying 13-16% organic growth, with EPS of $1.85-$1.95. Risks include potential CMS cuts to the IPPS for FY2025, but our 45% exposure to procedure-based reimbursement mitigates this. In summary, Q2 is about execution: launching game-changing tech, expanding smartly, and running lean. We're confident this sets the stage for our FY2024 goal of 15%+ growth and 25%+ ROIC.

Sarah Kline:
Excellent overview, David. Thank you. Now, let's talk about competitive dynamics and market share trends. David, over to you.

David Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. Competitive dynamics and market share trends continue to shape our trajectory in the $520 billion global medical devices market, projected to grow at a 5.8% CAGR through 2028 according to recent Grand View Research data. In our core franchises—cardiovascular interventions, orthopedics, and neuromodulation—we're not just participating in this growth; we're outpacing it through disciplined execution, innovation, and a relentless focus on clinical differentiation.

Let me start with the big picture. Q1 marked our 11th consecutive quarter of market share expansion across our top three segments, which collectively represent 72% of our revenue. We gained 150 basis points globally, reaching an estimated 14.2% share in structural heart devices—up from 12.1% a year ago—driven by our next-gen TAVR platform, the ApexValve Pro, which captured 22% of U.S. TAVR procedures in Q1 per DAR registry data. This outperforms the segment's 14% year-over-year growth, fueled by an aging demographic and expanding indications for intermediate-risk patients.

Competitively, the landscape remains fragmented but intensifying. Medtronic holds a commanding 28% share in cardiovascular rhythm management with their Micra leadless pacemaker iterations, but we've clawed back 80 basis points in that subcategory to 11.5% through our miniaturized Asserta CRM platform, which boasts a 97% implant success rate and 30% smaller footprint than legacy devices. Boston Scientific's Watchman FLX continues to pressure our LAAO franchise, where they command 35% U.S. share, but our Sentinel LAA occluder—now with AI-enhanced imaging integration—reversed a 2% share erosion from last year, delivering 18% procedural growth in Europe.

In orthopedics, a $55 billion addressable market growing at 4.9% CAGR, we're navigating a post-COVID elective recovery that's uneven. Stryker's Mako robotic-arm system dominates at 42% of U.S. robotic knee procedures, but our OrthoNav 4.0 system—launched mid-year with haptic feedback and machine-learning optimized implant planning—propelled us to 16.8% share in robotic-assisted hips, a 220 basis points gain quarter-over-quarter. This is critical as robotics penetration hits 25% in the U.S. but lags at 12% in Europe due to reimbursement hurdles. Zimmer Biomet's ROSA platform is a worthy challenger, yet our system's sub-1% revision rate at 24 months gives us a clear edge in value-based care models like CMS's Bundled Payments for Care Improvement.

Regionally, dynamics vary sharply. In the U.S., which accounts for 48% of our sales, we're at peak share momentum: 19.4% in structural heart, up 3.1 points year-over-year, outpacing Abbott's Navitor TAVR by emphasizing our valve's 2.1% annualized leak rate versus their 3.4%. Pricing remains stable at a 4% premium to peers, supported by 92% hospital adoption in high-volume centers. Europe, 28% of revenue, saw us gain 1.8 points to 13.6% overall, despite CE Mark delays for competitors like Edwards Lifesciences' SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA. Our early-mover advantage in Germany's DRG system—where we've secured preferred status in 65% of top cath labs—drove 16% constant-currency growth amid a 9% market expansion.

Asia-Pacific, our fastest-growing region at 22% of sales, presents both opportunity and headwinds. China's structural heart market is exploding at 22% CAGR to $2.5 billion by 2027, per Frost & Sullivan, but local players like Peijia Medical and Venus Medtech are aggressive with NMPA-approved TAVR valves priced 40-50% below ours. We've countered with a JV partnership in Shanghai, localizing assembly for our ApexValve Lite, capturing 8.2% share in Shanghai and Guangdong hubs—up from 4.1%—while navigating the Made in China 2025 procurement preferences. In Japan, PMDA approval for our Asserta CRM has us at 12% share, trailing Medtronic's 31% but accelerating via JMDN reimbursement parity.

Emerging markets like India and Brazil, 7% of revenue, are wild cards. Low penetration—under 5% for TAVR—offers upside, but regulatory harmonization lags. Our $50 million investment in a Brazil manufacturing facility has stabilized supply post-pandemic disruptions, yielding 310 basis points share gains to 9.7% in neuromodulation, where our Infuse SCS system for chronic pain outperforms Nevro's HF10 on battery life, 12 years versus 10.

Strategically, we're leveraging three pillars to sustain this momentum. First, technical innovation: Q1 R&D spend hit 14.2% of revenue, up 190 basis points year-over-year, funding 12 IDE approvals and our AI-driven Predicta platform, which integrates real-time procedural analytics to reduce fluoroscopy time by 28%—a differentiator against Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci in hybrid ORs. We're also advancing our bioresorbable stent portfolio, targeting a 2025 launch to disrupt the $8 billion coronary market dominated by Boston Scientific's Synergy.

Second, M&A and partnerships: The $1.2 billion acquisition of NeuroStim Dynamics bolsters our neuromodulation to 22% share, adding closed-loop DBS tech competitive with Medtronic's Percept PC. We've inked co-development deals with Philips for imaging integration, addressing interoperability gaps that plague 30% of hybrid procedures.

Third, commercial excellence: Our Voyager360 sales force optimization—using Salesforce Einstein AI—boosted door-to-door conversion by 17%, while surgeon education programs reached 4,200 KOLs, fostering loyalty amid competitor poaching. Supply chain resilience is key too; dual-sourcing titanium for orthopedics mitigated the 2023 rare earth shortages that hit J&J's DePuy by 8% output.

Risks include reimbursement cliffs like the U.S. TAVR pass-through expiration in 2025, which could compress ASPs by 5-7%, and biosimilar erosion in cardiology. But our 65% gross margins—top decile—give us pricing power, and a $3.2 billion cash pile funds buybacks or bolt-ons. In summary, we're gaining share in a consolidating market by out-innovating incumbents, localizing smartly, and executing flawlessly. This positions us for 8-10% organic growth in FY24, well above industry averages.

Sarah Kline:
Thanks, David—strong momentum there. Moving on to inventory management and working capital optimization. David?

David Patel:
Good morning again, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our inventory management and working capital optimization efforts, which have been a cornerstone of our operational excellence strategy amid ongoing headwinds in the medical devices sector. As you know, our industry faces unique challenges: stringent FDA and EU MDR regulations demanding lot-level traceability and sterility validation, supply chain volatility from resin shortages and semiconductor constraints—echoing the disruptions that hit peers like Abbott and Boston Scientific last year—and the need to balance just-in-time delivery for high-margin products like our next-gen TAVR valves and robotic-assisted surgical systems, akin to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci platforms.

Let me start with the headline numbers, which underscore the tangible impact of our initiatives. In Q1, we reduced our Days Inventory Outstanding, or DIO, to 98 days—a 15% improvement from 115 days in Q1 2023 and a sequential drop of 7 days from Q4 2023. This drove inventory turns up to 3.7x annually, from 3.1x a year ago, putting us ahead of the industry median of 3.2x per the latest Deloitte Medical Devices Benchmarking Report. On working capital, our Cash Conversion Cycle tightened to 72 days, down from 92 days year-over-year, primarily through DIO compression and a modest 2-day extension in Days Payable Outstanding to 68 days via optimized vendor terms. This freed up $285 million in cash flow from operations in the first half—representing a 22% year-over-year increase—and directly funded our $450 million in R&D for electrophysiology catheters and neuromodulation devices without dipping further into our revolver.

Regionally, our performance varies but shows consistent progress. In the U.S., which accounts for 52% of our revenue, DIO stands at a lean 92 days, bolstered by our consignment inventory model with top IDNs like Kaiser Permanente and HCA Healthcare. We've shifted 28% of our orthopedic implant inventory—think our flagship knee and hip systems—to vendor-managed consignment, reducing our on-hand stock by $120 million while maintaining 99.2% fill rates. This mirrors Stryker's successful playbook but with our proprietary RFID-enabled trays for real-time visibility.

In Europe, comprising 28% of sales, EU MDR recertification delays pushed DIO to 110 days, but we've clawed it back 12% year-over-year through localized manufacturing at our Galway, Ireland facility. Here, we've implemented AI-driven demand sensing via our SAP S/4HANA ERP integrated with Blue Yonder forecasting tools, which improved forecast accuracy for cardiovascular stents from 78% to 92%. This mitigated the 15-20% inventory buildup we saw industry-wide last year due to Notified Body bottlenecks.

Asia-Pacific, our fastest-growing region at 20% of revenue with 18% year-over-year growth, saw DIO at 102 days despite China tariff escalations and local content mandates. Strategic stockpiling of critical components like bioresorbable polymers—up 8% in safety stock—protected against Red Sea shipping disruptions, but our JIT partnerships with TSMC for device chips kept working capital efficient.

Now, turning to the technical initiatives powering these gains. First, our Enterprise Inventory Optimization Program, launched Q4 2023, leverages machine learning algorithms on 2.5 petabytes of historical data to dynamically adjust safety stock levels. For ABC-classified SKUs—where A items like our ApexValve TAVR systems represent 20% of inventory but 75% of value—we've cut excess by 25% using Monte Carlo simulations for demand variability. We've also rolled out blockchain-based traceability pilots with suppliers like DuPont for PEEK polymers, ensuring 100% compliance with UDI requirements and reducing obsolescence write-downs from $45 million in 2023 to under $20 million run-rate.

Second, supplier collaboration is key. Through Vendor Managed Inventory with 65% of our top-20 suppliers—including resin giants like Covestro—we've extended payment terms to 75 days on average while granting them portal access to our demand signals. This VMI model now covers 35% of raw materials, slashing our Days Sales of Inventory for Class B consumables like laparoscopic trocars by 18 days.

Strategically, these efforts align with our Resilient Growth 2027 framework. In a market where med device COGS inflation hit 6-8% from raw material pressures—per PwC's latest outlook—we're targeting sub-95 DIO by year-end through full GenAI adoption for scenario planning, including climate-risk modeling for supply chains. This not only de-risks our 12-15% EPS growth guidance but positions us for M&A, like our recent tuck-in of a digital surgery analytics firm to enhance inventory predictive analytics.

Looking ahead, we expect Q2 DIO at 95 days, with CCC under 70, generating another $150 million in free cash flow. Risks remain—geopolitical tensions could add 5-7 DIO if chip lead times stretch beyond 24 weeks—but our diversified sourcing from Vietnam and Mexico mitigates this. In summary, our disciplined inventory and working capital discipline has transformed a historical drag—where med device peers averaged 110+ DIO—into a competitive moat, fueling margin expansion to 68% gross margins and ROIC above 15%.

Sarah Kline:
Impressive progress, David. Finally, on FDA approvals and CE marks obtained this quarter—milestones that represent a pivotal inflection point for our growth in the $120 billion global structural heart and peripheral vascular devices market. Let me highlight our remarkable progress here.

We secured FDA 510(k) clearance for our next-generation DynaFlow Drug-Eluting Stent platform, specifically the DynaFlow Ultra model, which features our proprietary bioresorbable polymer matrix and enhanced radial strength for superior deliverability in complex calcified lesions. This clearance was supported by benchtop data showing 25% improved trackability versus our prior iteration and predicate devices like the Boston Scientific Synergy XD, alongside non-clinical animal studies demonstrating 95% strut coverage at 30 days—well above the industry benchmark of 85% set by recent ORBITA-2 trial meta-analyses.

Complementing that, we received full PMA approval for our PulseGuard TAVR system, our self-expanding, repositionable transcatheter aortic valve replacement platform with integrated leaflet motion monitoring via embedded inertial sensors. This is our first PMA in structural heart, backed by our pivotal ENVISION IDE trial, which enrolled 450 high-risk surgical patients across 35 U.S. centers. Topline data showed a 1.8% all-cause 30-day mortality rate—statistically superior to the 2.4% benchmark from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/ACC TVT Registry for similar-risk cohorts—and a 97% technical success rate per VARC-3 criteria. We're particularly proud of the 12-month echo follow-up, revealing just 1.2% moderate or greater paravalvular leak, a 40% improvement over legacy supra-annular valves like Medtronic's CoreValve Evolut.

On the international front, both the DynaFlow Ultra and PulseGuard received CE Mark certification under the stringent EU MDR 2017/745 framework—the first MDR-cleared TAVR in our portfolio. This was no small feat; MDR Notified Body scrutiny has delayed over 60% of legacy CE renewals since 2021, per Emergo by UL data. Our submissions leveraged our ISO 13485:2016 QMS enhancements and post-market surveillance from our 5,000-patient EU registry, achieving first-cycle approval in under 18 months—half the industry average.

Translating these into financial impact, these approvals unlock a combined $8.5 billion addressable market: $4.2 billion U.S. DES segment, where we're targeting 8-10% share by FY26 through our 350-person direct U.S. sales force, and $4.3 billion global TAVR market growing at 22% CAGR per Grand View Research. We project these launches to contribute $285 million in incremental revenue in FY25—$180 million from PulseGuard TAVR alone—representing 22% of our total revenue guidance midpoint. Early U.S. limited market release for PulseGuard has already secured $45 million in confirmed orders from top-tier centers like Cleveland Clinic and Mount Sinai, with Q4 inventory builds supporting a 150% ramp in implant volumes.

Regionally, the CE Marks position us for accelerated EU penetration, where TAVR volumes grew 28% year-over-year in H1 2024 per EPIC Alliance data, outpacing the U.S. at 18%. We've activated 120 EU accounts, including key reimbursable pathways in Germany via DiGA fast-track and France's HAS listing, expecting €120 million in Eurozone sales next year. Looking East, we're filing for Japan PMDA approval on PulseGuard in Q1 2025, leveraging mutual recognition with FDA data, which could tap into Japan's $1.2 billion TAVR market constrained by single-digit penetration.

From a technical standpoint, these successes stem from our $165 million R&D investment this year—up 35% year-over-year—focusing on AI-driven lesion preparation via our VascuAI platform, which integrates OCT imaging with predictive analytics for 30% faster procedural times. We've also advanced three more assets in our 12-product pipeline: the DynaFlow DCB for below-the-knee PAD, under FDA breakthrough designation with Breakthrough Devices Program fast-tracking, and our robotic-assisted peripheral atherectomy system in EU clinicals.

Strategically, these milestones de-risk our 45% organic growth algorithm through 2027. We're mitigating regulatory headwinds—like FDA's increased PMA inspection cadence, up 50% post-2023—and capitalizing on tailwinds such as the Biden Administration's $50 million cardiac device innovation fund. Competitively, we outpace Abbott's recent Navitor TAVR clearance by six months to market, and our cost structure—25% below peers on COGS via U.S. manufacturing resilience—supports 65% gross margins on new launches. These FDA and CE achievements aren't just checkboxes; they're launchpads for sustained leadership in high-growth medtech segments. Our regulatory team, bolstered by ex-Medtronic hires, has now delivered seven clearances in 18 months—a 3x acceleration. This positions MedTech Innovations to harvest $1.2 billion in cumulative revenue from the pipeline by 2028, while advancing our mission to redefine patient outcomes in cardiovascular care.

I will now turn the call over to David for a review of our financial results.

David Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter. Let me walk through the key details.

Starting with the top line, Q1 revenue reached $1.2 billion, up 14% year-over-year on an organic basis, driven by 18% growth in structural heart, 22% in neuromodulation, and solid contributions from orthopedics. U.S. revenue was $745 million, or 62% of total, up 16%; EMEA at 24%, and APAC up 28%. Product revenue mix remained strong, with high-margin devices like TAVR and robotics leading the way.

On the bottom line, adjusted gross margins expanded 210 basis points to 68.2%, benefiting from multi-sourcing, automation, and favorable mix. Operating expenses were disciplined: R&D at 14.2% of revenue, up due to pipeline investments; SG&A compressed through zero-based budgeting and sales force efficiency. Adjusted operating income rose 20% to $320 million, with EPS of $1.72, beating consensus by $0.07.

Balance sheet remains robust: $3.2 billion in cash, DIO at 98 days, CCC at 72 days, generating $285 million in operating cash flow. We repurchased $150 million in shares and raised our dividend 8%.

For guidance, we're raising FY2024 revenue to $5.15-$5.25 billion, 14-16% organic growth, with adjusted EPS of $7.40-$7.60. Q2 revenues $1.28-$1.32 billion, 13-16% organic, EPS $1.85-$1.95. Margins to expand further to 69%+, ROIC over 25%. Key assumptions include stable reimbursement, supply chain continuity, and launch ramps from new clearances.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Sarah for Q&A.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, David. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star then one on your telephone. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Sarah, on the strategic priorities for Q2, particularly the PrecisionNav 3.0 launch and APAC expansion—how do you see the competitive response from Medtronic and Zimmer Biomet, and what's the risk to your 25% attach rate target?

Sarah Kline:
Thanks, Emily. Great question. Medtronic and Zimmer are formidable, but our AI-driven 3D fusion gives PrecisionNav a clear edge in spinal precision, with early surgeon feedback showing 20% faster procedures. We've locked in pilots with 50 centers via VAC wins, and our attach rate builds on existing OrthoNav adoption. APAC localization mitigates tariff risks, and we're confident in the $45 million ramp. Risks are low given diversified installs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Singh with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Singh:
Hi team, solid inventory work—DIO down to 98 days is impressive. David, can you elaborate on the AI demand sensing rollout in Europe and how it factors into Q2 CCC guidance under 70 days?

David Patel:
Hi Raj, thanks. The SAP-Blue Yonder integration has boosted forecast accuracy to 92% for stents, directly cutting EU DIO by 12% despite MDR delays. VMI with Covestro and others extends DPO, and GenAI scenario planning handles volatility. Q2 CCC under 70 assumes steady supplier terms and no major disruptions—our diversified sourcing gives us buffer. This supports $150 million FCF.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim:
Thanks. Lisa, on the FDA PMA for PulseGuard TAVR—those ENVISION trial stats are outstanding. How does the inertial sensor tech integrate with existing hybrid ORs, and what's the timeline for full commercial rollout?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Laura. The embedded sensors provide real-time leaflet monitoring, reducing PVL to 1.2% via predictive adjustments—unique in the market. VascuAI compatibility ensures seamless hybrid OR integration with Philips and Siemens systems, cutting fluoro by 30%. Limited release now, full U.S. ramp Q3 with 150% volume growth, EU via CE Mark already activating 120 accounts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Torres with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Torres:
Congrats on share gains. Sarah, in competitive dynamics, China JV for ApexValve Lite—how are you navigating local players like Peijia, and does the 8.2% share accelerate with NRDL?

Sarah Kline:
Mike, thanks. Peijia's pricing is aggressive, but our Lite version matches on performance with U.S.-proven data, and NRDL inclusion for ICDs/TAVR drives pull-through. Shanghai JV localizes 40%, aligning with Made in China 2025, up from 4.1% share. Expect 12% by 2025 on 22% market CAGR—partnerships de-risk execution.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to reiterate our confidence in the long-term growth potential of MedTech Innovations. We are committed to delivering innovative medical device solutions that improve patient outcomes and create value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
